research_summary.objective: Build an India-specific, source-traceable emergency-contact knowledge base covering national, state, Union Territory, district, and service-specific emergency routing.
major_findings: No live official source was opened and verified in this research pass.
No emergency number has been admitted into the production corpus because emergency numbers must not be inferred from memory or search snippets.
National, state, Union Territory, district, and service-specific emergency information remains unresolved pending live verification.
india_specific_gaps: Current operational status and geographic coverage of national integrated emergency services.
Current police, ambulance, fire, disaster-management, highway, state, Union Territory, and district emergency contacts.
Legacy-number status and migration or redirection arrangements.
Official confirmation of toll-free, mobile-access, SIM, balance, language, and call-routing characteristics.
research_summary.freshness_recommendation: Use a hybrid approach: store only verified emergency-number records with source and verification metadata, refresh them periodically from official sources, and use live official-source lookup or an actively maintained directory for state, Union Territory, district, and local contacts. Do not rely on an undated static RAG record as the sole source for emergency numbers.

implementation_notes: Do not ingest any emergency number until the exact official source page or document has been opened and verified.

Every emergency-number record should include service_type, emergency_type, phone_number, region, state, district, jurisdiction, source_id, authority_level, active_status, verification_date, last_updated, review_due_date, language, and legacy_status.
National emergency numbers should be represented separately from state, Union Territory, district, local police, ambulance, fire, and highway numbers.
A regional number must never be returned without confirming the user's state and, where necessary, district or route.
If a regional number is unavailable or stale, RAAHAT should use only a currently verified national fallback; it should not invent or infer a local number.
Legacy numbers should be stored separately from active numbers and must never be returned as the primary contact unless current official operation is explicitly verified.
District and local contacts should preferably be retrieved from actively maintained official sources rather than stored permanently as static RAG facts.
Emergency-number records require periodic refresh and visible verification timestamps.
International emergency numbers should not be included in the Indian emergency-number corpus.
The current dataset contains no production-ready emergency-number records because no live official sources were verified in this pass.
